holidays.name: National Margarita Day
holidays.description: Salt the rim and raise a glass. February 22 is the day for the tequila, lime and orange liqueur cocktail. You can have it on the rocks, blended or spicy, and fans take the chance to try every variation.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that has grown through bars, restaurants and social media. Its roots are in the margarita's mid-20th-century rise as one of America's favorite cocktails.
holidays.funFact: There are many competing stories about who invented the margarita. Claimed inventors include a Tijuana restaurateur, a Texas socialite and a California bartender, and none of the claims has been settled.

holidays.name: National Walking the Dog Day
holidays.description: This day is a reminder to clip on the leash and take your four-legged friend out for a stroll. The walk is good for your pup's health, and it gives you some fresh air and exercise too.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is celebrated by dog lovers each February 22 and encourages regular walks for pets and their people.
holidays.funFact: For many dogs, the sniffing on a walk is mentally tiring in a good way. A sniff-heavy stroll can wear out a dog about as much as a faster, sniff-free one.

holidays.name: World Thinking Day
holidays.description: Girl Guides and Girl Scouts around the world use this day to think about global friendship, take part in service projects and speak up for causes they care about. Each year has a theme, and troops hold events and swap greetings with groups in other countries.
holidays.origin: It began in 1926, when Girl Guides and Girl Scouts chose a day to honor international friendship. February 22 was picked because it is the birthday of both Robert Baden-Powell, founder of the Scout movement, and his wife Olave, who was a Guiding leader.
holidays.funFact: Robert and Olave Baden-Powell were born on the same calendar date, February 22, though 32 years apart. That shared birthday is why the day is celebrated.
